items.text: After an extraordinary [[p:North Atlantic Council]] session on 23 Nov over the three Russian cruise missiles that fell in Poland, Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski said NATO is sending an [[p:NATO Airborne Early Warning & Control Force|AWACS]] early-warning aircraft to Poland at once. Warsaw's requests for F-35s and more ground-based air defence under [[e:Eastern Sentry]] are still being evaluated, and no communiqué was reported. SACEUR [[p:Alexus Grynkewich]] is reviewing the alliance's posture; [[p:Mark Rutte]] said he would not speculate on whether the strike was intentional.
items.notes: No NATO primary release found; AWACS decision reported via Polish officials. Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz says allied early-warning aircraft are already over Poland.

items.text: NATO members' intelligence services have concluded that Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit this year, German media report, according to Reuters. The device was reportedly assembled several years ago and is kept in the Moscow region. Moscow has not commented on the report; a nuclear weapon in orbit would breach the [[e:Outer Space Treaty]] {{note: 1967 treaty, drafted at the UN and signed by the US, UK and Soviet Union, that bans nuclear weapons in orbit.}}.
items.notes: Unnamed intelligence sources via German media; not confirmed by NATO or any government.

items.text: Drones struck a residential area of Khartoum and UN premises before dawn on 22 Nov, the first reported attack on a UN compound in the capital since the army retook it in 2025. Sudan Tribune reports at least four killed near the city, including a 10-year-old. OCHA says the strikes were reportedly launched by the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]]; Sudanese military sources claim the drones took off from Bahir Dar airport in Ethiopia, which Addis Ababa has denied in the past. UN coordinator Denise Brown called for an end to the drone supply and a humanitarian truce.
items.notes: Ethiopian launch site is a Sudanese army claim, unverified. Sudan's Sovereignty Council earlier claimed 70 attacks from Ethiopia between Feb and Oct.

items.text: Foreign ministry spokesman [[p:Esmaeil Baghaei]] called the US naval blockade military aggression and said Iran will use 'all available means' against it, citing self-defence under the UN Charter. This came after [[p:Donald Trump]] told Fox News that Iranian ships trying to break the [[e:2026 United States naval blockade of Iran|blockade]] would go to the bottom of the sea. Baghaei said Hormuz reopens only if Washington lifts sanctions, ends the blockade and honours the [[e:Islamabad Talks|Islamabad]] memorandum; he dismissed reports of Iranian tankers loading oil as speculation.
items.notes: Sources differ on Araghchi's reopening timeline: 'within two days' (Al Jazeera, CBS) vs 'within two hours' (Euronews). Tasnim says plans to break the blockade are being drawn up but none announced.

items.text: A Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on 20 Nov, Deputy FM [[p:Kazem Gharibabadi]] said. FM [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] says messages pass through mediators but discussing Hormuz is pointless until Iran's demands are met. Trump says he wants a 'permanent' deal and posted that Iran had fired more drones and missiles in the past week than at any time in over a year, to no effect. Qatar's prime minister was expected to meet [[p:Marco Rubio]] on 23 Nov.
items.notes: Outcome of the Qatar PM–Rubio meeting not found at time of logging. Ynet (via Gulf News) reports a possible US strike on Iran postponed by at least a week; unverified.

items.text: The Joint Maritime Information Centre counts seven oil tankers hit since 16 Nov, three of them 8–17 nautical miles off Khasab, Oman, on 20–21 Nov. A Jordanian sailor is missing and the UAE and Oman are searching. Brent was above $92 on 23 Nov; Etihad has cancelled flights to 30 Nov and Iranian airlines have suspended UAE routes.

Iranian state TV showed a new two-missile launcher and base during a visit by IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi and IRGC Air Force commander Majid Mousavi; IRGC deputy Mostafa Izadi said any threat would be answered 'without geographical limitations'. The US rejects an Iranian claim to have hit an American fighter jet.
items.notes: No independent verification of the launcher footage.

items.text: An airstrike on two Houthi vehicles in a frontline area of Lahj also hit a passing truck and bus, killing 26, local officials told AFP: 12 [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] fighters and 14 civilians. The officials blamed coalition warplanes and the Houthis blamed the Saudi air force, vowing a response; government forces spokesman Majed al-Nazli said the Houthis carried out the attack themselves.
items.notes: Attribution disputed three ways; AFP does not resolve it.

items.text: Houthi reinforcements massed on the Al-Bayda–Abyan front, and aircraft struck them for three days up to 21 Nov at the Thara pass and in the Al-Kawr mountains north of Loder, military sources and residents say. A government-aligned politician says the aim is to encircle Aden rather than storm it. The government reshuffled its Abyan commanders, and Southern forces sent reinforcements.
items.notes: Anonymous military sources; operator of the aircraft not named. UNHCR warned about the Kharaz camp (about 9,600 mostly Somali and Ethiopian refugees) near the front.

items.text: Houthi media say a Saudi strike on a telecommunications building in Hodeidah killed 10 to 17 people; Riyadh did not comment. A day earlier the coalition said it intercepted Houthi drones towards Riyadh and a ballistic missile aimed at the Red Sea coast.
items.notes: Toll differs between Houthi outlets: 17 (telecoms ministry) vs 10 (Al-Masirah).

items.text: The Houthis have deployed more informants and plainclothes agents across Sanaa in recent days and accuse residents of spying for the government and the coalition, local sources tell Asharq Al-Awsat.

The UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt and the Arab League condemned the Iranian strike that set fire to a civilian industrial site in Bahrain on 21 Nov and injured two, one critically. Bahrain separately rejected UN claims that recent arrests were religiously motivated.

[[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s Yashar party and [[p:Likud]] resumed coalition talks on 22 Nov after Eisenkot called a 'marathon' of meetings; they ended without a deal but set a follow-up. Likud's conditions include no Arab parties, rejection of Palestinian statehood and keeping 'security zones' in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza. [[p:Naftali Bennett]] backs a unity government under Eisenkot without [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]], and Eisenkot says he will put a minority 'national emergency government' to a vote if talks fail; Kan reports he may spring the vote at short notice.
items.notes: Times of Israel reports Eisenkot and Bennett split over giving Likud a deadline. Kan's timing ('within a day or two' vs 'coming weeks') is inconsistent.

items.text: Settlers torched vehicles and homes in villages near Ramallah over the weekend and sprayed slogans such as 'Revenge' and 'Death to Arabs'. Eisenkot called it 'Jewish terrorism' and blamed ministers [[p:Itamar Ben-Gvir]] and [[p:Bezalel Smotrich]]. Separately, an IDF raid in Yabed was filmed with a detained man zip-tied on the floor; the IDF did not comment.
items.notes: Reuters article read via the Just Security digest summary.

items.text: Israel's central Gaza operation, launched on 18 Nov near Nuseirat, Bureij and Maghazi, was followed by daily drone strikes: at least seven were killed on 20 Nov, four of them in Bureij. On 21 Nov a strike killed three in a vehicle carrying food with [[p:World Central Kitchen]] papers; WCK says it was not theirs, and the IDF says it targeted [[p:Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] members. [[p:Hamas]] calls the operation a ceasefire violation; the IDF says it removed a threat near the 'yellow line'.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: Hamas says evacuation orders were forced; Al Jazeera reporter Hind Khoudary says no evacuation order was issued. Gaza Health Ministry figures.

items.text: The [[p:United Nations Security Council|Security Council]] reaffirmed support for [[p:United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]] six weeks before its mandate ends on 31 Dec but named no successor. Washington proposes keeping [[e:United Nations Security Council Resolution 1701|Resolution 1701]] with amendments, France is drafting a new resolution, and Beirut wants any force under UN authority. Unknown gunmen fired about a dozen rounds at a UNIFIL patrol near Tyre; no one was hurt.
items.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation
items.notes: Closed consultations on a replacement expected in New York the following week.

items.text: Israel struck the entrances of a former [[p:Hezbollah]] missile-production site at Janta in the Bekaa, its second Bekaa strike that week; NNA reported five airstrikes. On 22 Nov the [[p:Lebanese Armed Forces|Lebanese army]] seized TNT and C-4 smuggled from Syria at Mashari al-Qaa and detained six Lebanese.
items.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation

items.text: Israeli raids in Quneitra and Deraa have intensified, and analysts expect the occupation of the south to continue whoever forms Israel's next government. The Arab Reform Initiative counted 678 ground incursions and 168 raids from January to September 2026; the [[p:Syrian Network for Human Rights]] says 35 Syrians detained by Israel are unaccounted for.

The Jurf al-Sakhar compromise came a day before the deadline, reportedly after [[p:Esmail Qaani]] of the IRGC's [[p:Quds Force]] intervened. An army brigade, a federal police brigade, an energy police regiment and two [[p:Popular Mobilization Forces|PMF]] brigades are deploying in phases while [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]] withdraws gradually. Analysts disagree on whether it is a real step or militias swapped for militias in uniform.
items.notes: Iranian mediation reported, not confirmed by Baghdad.

items.text: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi made his first visit to Egypt since taking office in May, meeting [[p:Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] and co-chairing the joint higher committee with [[p:Mostafa Madbouly]].

The [[p:Council of State (Turkey)|Council of State]] upheld the revocation of [[p:Ekrem İmamoğlu]]'s university degree, which the constitution requires of presidential candidates, Sabah reports; his lawyers say they have not been notified. A day earlier an Ankara court gave him and eight others over two years each over the 2023 CHP leadership vote, with political bans if upheld. The [[p:Constitutional Court of Turkey|Constitutional Court]] takes up his pretrial detention on 26 Nov.
items.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown
items.notes: Degree ruling reported by pro-government Sabah; not yet formally served.
